newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives to tighten up on food safety.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives to tighten up on food safety.

text.p: Britain's Conservative Party said it would tighten up control of food safety if it remains in government after May Day elections.
In its election manifesto, the party said it would appoint "a powerful and independent chief food safety adviser and food safety council to advise government."

Britain has been beset with food-related health crises over the past year. BSE, or mad cow disease, has led to British beef being shunned abroad and an outbreak of E-Coli in Scotland has now claimed 20 lives.
Last month, Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg was accused of suppressing a report on unhealthy conditions in abattoirs, sparked by the E-Coli crisis.

The Tory manifesto pledged support to the beef industry until its strength is restored. "We will vigorously pursue the eradication of BSE in the United Kingdom. We will spare no efforts in our fight against the unwarranted ban on British beef exports."
The Conservatives said they would stand firm in the European Union to stop quota hopping in the fisheries industry and to prevent boats from other countries from using British fishing quotas.

"We will also continue to push for fundamental reform of the Common Agricultural Policy, moving...to measures that will give our farmers the opportunity to compete while safeguarding the rural environment," the manifesto said.
